issue_context.title: Verisure forgets username/password
issue_context.body:
### The problem

After running for a few hours or sometimes days, it seems like the integration is forgetting the username/password.

A notification is issued that the integration needs reconfiguration and the integration appears in red at the top of the integrations page.

When trying to just reload the integration, it gives the same error.

Clicking "Reconfigure" and adding the username and password again solves the problem.





### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2023.5.4

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

Unknown

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Verisure

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/verisure/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Typical log-entries when the problem starts:

(...)

2023-06-03 14:09:13.281 DEBUG (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.verisure] Finished fetching verisure data in 0.898 seconds (success: True)
2023-06-03 14:10:13.849 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.verisure] Could not log in to verisure, Invalid response, status code: 401 - Data: {"errorGroup": "UNAUTHORIZED","errorCo
de": "AUT_00001","errorMessage": "Username/password does not match any valid login"}                                                                                                          
2023-06-03 14:10:13.853 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.verisure] Authentication failed while fetching verisure data: Could not log in to verisure
```

When trying to just reload the integration, it gives the same error:

```
2023-06-04 10:09:07.841 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.verisure] Could not log in to verisure, Invalid response, status code: 401 - Data: {"errorGroup": "UNAUTHORIZED","errorCode": "AUT_00001","errorMessage": "Username/password does not match any valid login"}
2023-06-04 10:09:07.867 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.config_entries] Config entry 'Xxxxxx  (Xxxxxx Xx)' for verisure integration not ready yet: Could not log in to verisure.; Retrying in background
2023-06-04 10:09:13.166 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.verisure] Could not log in to verisure, Invalid response, status code: 401 - Data: {"errorGroup": "UNAUTHORIZED","errorCode": "AUT_00001","errorMessage": "Session has expired"}
2023-06-04 10:09:23.391 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.verisure] Could not log in to verisure, Invalid response, status code: 401 - Data: {"errorGroup": "UNAUTHORIZED","errorCode": "AUT_00001","errorMessage": "Username/password does not match any valid login"}

```

Clicking "Reconfigure" and adding the username and password again solves the problem.

```

@niro1987 - no, this was just a hiccup today. I think the underlying complaint of having to reauthenticate more often than it used to be needed in the past is still there (I have too been experiencing this for the last few weeks). But it could be something new on Verisure side of things.

Logically speaking the issue is with the integration and not with Verisure:
- We provide the password
- At some point the integration decides that is no longer valid and forgets it
- We provide the same password :)

So I assume that sometimes the integration receives an error code that is interpreted as "the password is no longer valid" and it throws it away to avoid endlessly trying with a wrong password... makes sense.

Probably tuning the above mechanism (correctly interpreting the error code, allow some grace period, ...) can make this issue go away.

HA doesn't throw away the username/password but after a failed attempt of updating the cookies, it does [mark the integration as invalid](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/2be5bab5e1deb648d2091a57fd4e28fd092bbe07/homeassistant/components/verisure/coordinator.py#LL70C1-L70C1), requiring a re-authentication.

In my dev environment I've replaced line 72 from this
```py
            raise ConfigEntryAuthFailed("Could not log in to verisure") from ex
```
to this
```py

```
hoping that I would see the error without the integration being marked for re-authentication.

The documentation is not very clear on those errors, at least as far as I can find, but i found this:
_"Raising ConfigEntryAuthFailed will cancel future updates and start a config flow with SOURCE_REAUTH (async_step_reauth)"_

This step seems to be implemented:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/4a8adae1464a919fc03af7a7df0efefa5af92852/homeassistant/components/verisure/config_flow.py#L174

But there might be a problem somwhere here:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/4a8adae1464a919fc03af7a7df0efefa5af92852/homeassistant/components/verisure/config_flow.py#L182-L239

Possibly addding some debug info in the "_confirm" function could show where it fails.

I am currently away and unable to do that in my own installation, but it might help.

Just looking at the code very quickly, it seems like everything in `_confirm()` is wrapped inside the `if user_input is not None:`, but user_input is not set in the call to the function, so unless something is going on behind the scenes, the `_confirm`  function does not actually do anything?

@persandstrom; investigating the issue, i think it's with the `wrapper`. When the request returns any status other then 200, the wrapper raises `ResponseError`, causing the integration the require re-authentication. Perhaps verisure no longer uses the `SYS_00004` message?

I have a fix that I would like to test, but seeing as I haven't been able to reproduce this error, is there anyone that is still facing this issue and that is willing and able to [setup a dev environment](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/development_environment/)?

```py
except VerisureError as ex:
    LOGGER.error("Could not log in to verisure, %s", ex)

```

The problem is that the reauth-function is not passed the username and password when the token expires. And when the integration is restarted, it will just try to use the expired token, and then run the reauth-function (which does not really reauthorise since it does not get the username and password).
When HA is restarted, the authentication starts from scratch (without trying the expired token), and that obviously works.
